Al-Fil 105:1–5 — offline summary

This is a brief summary of Ibn Kathir’s explanation, rather than the full commentary.

Ibn Kathir recounts Abrahah’s expedition against the Ka‘bah. After taking control of Yemen, Abrahah built a church and sought to divert the Arabs’ pilgrimage there. He later marched towards Makkah with an army and elephants, intending to destroy the Ka‘bah.

‘Abdul-Muttalib recovered his camels from Abrahah and urged the people of Makkah to seek safety in the mountains. When the army prepared to advance, its elephant refused to proceed towards Makkah. Allah sent flocks of birds carrying stones, and the attacking force was defeated.

The commentary explains that the final verse compares the destroyed army to the remains of crops consumed by animals. Ibn Kathir presents this event as Allah’s protection of His Sacred House and a blessing recalled to Quraysh.
